molarMassRef: PubChem CID 6013 (Testosterone), C19H28O2, 288.4 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6013 . Conversion: 1 nmol/L = 28.84 ng/dL.

refDefault.ageNote: Harmonized, CDC-standardized reference range derived from healthy non-obese men aged 19-39y; applied to healthy adult men. Levels decline with age/adiposity.
refDefault.note: 264-916 ng/dL = 9.2-31.8 nmol/L (matches patient lab-printed 9.20-31.80 nmol/L). Hypogonadism is commonly diagnosed below ~300 ng/dL (Endocrine Society / AUA). Draw morning, fasting; confirm low values on a repeat morning sample.

references.organization: Endocrine Society (Travison TG et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab)
references.document: Harmonized Reference Ranges for Circulating Testosterone Levels in Men of Four Cohort Studies in the United States and Europe
references.quote: The harmonized normal range in healthy nonobese men 19 to 39 years old was 264 to 916 ng/dL (9.2 to 31.8 nmol/L).

references.document: Landmark Study Defines Normal Ranges for Testosterone Levels (news release)
references.quote: Normal testosterone levels range from 264 to 916 ng/dL in men 19 to 39 years old who are not obese.

references.document: Testosterone Therapy in Men With Hypogonadism: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline
references.quote: We recommend making a diagnosis of hypogonadism only in men with symptoms and signs consistent with testosterone deficiency and unequivocally and consistently low serum total testosterone... a total testosterone level below 300 ng/dL is commonly used as a diagnostic threshold.

why: Primary readout of Leydig-cell androgen output and the core analyte of the HPG axis; screens for hypogonadism (low libido, fatigue, low mood, relevant to a ~43y male). Total T is the recommended first-line test; interpret with SHBG when binding is abnormal.

molarMassRef: Same molecule as total testosterone; PubChem CID 6013, 288.4 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/6013

refDefault.ageNote: Adult male (direct analog immunoassay range as printed by patient lab).
refDefault.note: UNCITED numeric range — taken from patient lab printout; direct analog immunoassay for free testosterone is NOT reliable (Endocrine Society 2018). Preferred: calculated free T (Vermeulen equation from total T + SHBG + albumin) or equilibrium dialysis, which correlate closely (r~0.99). Do not use this direct value for clinical decisions when SHBG is abnormal.

references.document: Testosterone Therapy in Men With Hypogonadism: An Endocrine Society Clinical Practice Guideline
references.quote: Free testosterone should be measured by equilibrium dialysis or calculated using an accurate formula; direct analog immunoassays for free testosterone are not reliable.

references.organization: Endocrine Society (Fiers T, Vermeulen A et al., J Clin Endocrinol Metab)
references.document: Reassessing Free-Testosterone Calculation by LC-MS/MS Direct Equilibrium Dialysis
references.quote: Calculated free testosterone using the Vermeulen equation correlates closely with equilibrium-dialysis free testosterone, unlike direct analog immunoassays.

why: Fraction of testosterone not bound to SHBG/albumin, biologically active. Useful when SHBG is abnormal and total T is borderline. However the direct analog immunoassay reported here is unreliable; a calculated free T (from this patient's total T, SHBG, albumin) is preferred.

loincs.longName: Sex hormone binding globulin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma
Sex hormone binding globulin [Moles/volume] in Serum or Plasma (older/alternate code)

molarMassRef: SHBG is a homodimeric plasma glycoprotein (~90-100 kDa); reported as a molar concentration by immunoassay calibration, no small-molecule molar mass applies.

refDefault.ageNote: Adult male (Mayo Clinic Laboratories reference interval).
refDefault.note: Patient lab printed a wider interval (14.5-95.0 nmol/L, assay-dependent). SHBG rises with age/thyroxine excess/liver disease and falls with obesity/insulin resistance; interpret total T in its context.

references.quote: Reference range for adult males: 10-57 nmol/L.

why: Principal transport protein for testosterone and estradiol; determines the free (bioavailable) fraction. Essential context for interpreting total testosterone and for computing calculated free testosterone. This patient is on levothyroxine (Euthyrox), which can raise SHBG.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 5757 (Estradiol), C18H24O2, 272.4 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/5757 . Conversion: 1 pg/mL = 3.671 pmol/L.

refDefault.ageNote: Adult male. Best measured by a sensitive LC-MS/MS assay in men (immunoassays are imprecise at male [low] concentrations).
refDefault.note: Matches patient lab-printed 10.00-40.00 pg/mL. Mayo LC-MS/MS (EEST) adult-male interval is reported in a similar low range (~10-40 pg/mL); use a sensitive/LC-MS/MS method for men.

references.document: Estradiol: Reference Range, Interpretation, Collection and Panels
references.quote: Adult male estradiol reference range is approximately 10-40 pg/mL.
Estradiol measured by high-sensitivity LC-MS/MS; low male-range concentrations require a sensitive method.

why: Main estrogen in men (aromatized from testosterone); important for bone, libido and gynecomastia risk. Elevated E2 with low T suggests increased aromatase activity/adiposity. Should be run by a sensitive/LC-MS/MS assay in males.

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 10635 (5-alpha-Dihydrotestosterone / Stanolone), C19H30O2, 290.4 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/10635 . Conversion: 1 nmol/L = 29.04 ng/dL; 1 ng/dL = 10 pg/mL.

refDefault.note: Mayo reports 11-95 ng/dL (0.38-3.27 nmol/L); expressed in pg/mL this is ~110-950 pg/mL (unit conversion, x10 from ng/dL). Patient lab printed 250-990 pg/mL, an assay-dependent interval. Measure by LC-MS/MS.

references.organization: Mayo Clinic Laboratories / Endocrine Reviews (Swerdloff RS et al.)
references.document: Dihydrotestosterone: Biochemistry, Physiology, and Clinical Implications of Elevated Blood Levels
references.quote: A normal DHT range of 11 to 95 ng/dL (0.38 to 3.27 nmol/L) has been published by a well-regarded commercial clinical laboratory (Mayo Medical Laboratories) that uses LC-MS/MS for the assay of DHT.

why: Most potent androgen, made from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase; drives prostate and scalp/hair effects. Useful in evaluating androgenic alopecia, 5-alpha-reductase issues, or monitoring 5-ARI therapy. LC-MS/MS is required for accuracy.

loincs.longName: Luteinizing hormone [Units/volume] in Serum or Plasma

molarMassRef: LH is a glycoprotein hormone (alpha/beta heterodimer, ~28-33 kDa) reported in international units (IU) against a WHO standard; no small-molecule molar mass applies.

refDefault.ageNote: Adult male (>=17y; Roche Elecsys / Mayo reference interval).
refDefault.note: Matches patient lab-printed 1.70-8.60 mIU/mL. mIU/mL is numerically equivalent to IU/L.

why: Pituitary gonadotropin that stimulates Leydig-cell testosterone production. Distinguishes primary (high LH) from secondary/central (low or inappropriately normal LH) hypogonadism when paired with total testosterone.

molarMassRef: FSH (follitropin) is a glycoprotein hormone (alpha/beta heterodimer, ~30 kDa) reported in international units (IU) against a WHO standard; no small-molecule molar mass applies.

refDefault.ageNote: Adult male (Roche Elecsys / Mayo reference interval).
refDefault.note: Matches patient lab-printed 1.50-12.40 mIU/mL. mIU/mL is numerically equivalent to IU/L.

references.quote: Adult males: 1.5-12.4 IU/L (Roche Elecsys reference interval).

why: Pituitary gonadotropin acting on Sertoli cells to support spermatogenesis. With LH it localizes the level of an HPG-axis lesion (testicular vs. pituitary/hypothalamic); elevated FSH signals seminiferous-tubule/germ-cell failure.

molarMassRef: Prolactin is a single-chain polypeptide hormone (~23 kDa); reported in ng/mL (mass) or mIU/L (IU vs WHO standard). Conversion used here: 1 ng/mL ~ 21.2 mIU/L (WHO 3rd IS 84/500). No small-molecule molar mass applies.

refDefault.note: Derived by converting the patient lab-printed Roche range 53-360 mIU/L using 1 ng/mL ~ 21.2 mIU/L -> ~2.5-17.0 ng/mL. Corroborated by published adult-male ranges (~3-13 ng/mL, Medscape). Note macroprolactin and stress/venipuncture can spuriously elevate PRL.

references.document: Prolactin: Reference Range, Interpretation, Collection and Panels
references.quote: Adult male prolactin reference range is approximately 3-13 ng/mL.
Prolactin, adult male reference interval (Roche immunoassay), reported in ng/mL.

why: Anterior-pituitary hormone; hyperprolactinemia (prolactinoma, dopamine-blocking drugs, hypothyroidism) suppresses GnRH/LH/FSH and causes secondary hypogonadism, low libido and infertility. Included to work up any low-testosterone finding. Relevant given this patient's stimulant (Concerta) and thyroid context.

loincs.longName: Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate [Mass/volume] in Serum or Plasma

molarMassRef: PubChem CID 12594 (Dehydroepiandrosterone sulfate / prasterone sulfate), C19H28O5S, 368.5 g/mol — https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/12594 . Conversion: 1 ug/dL = 0.02714 umol/L.

refDefault.ageNote: Adult male, age 40-49y band (DHEA-S is strongly age-banded and declines with age).
refDefault.note: The patient lab-printed interval (25.00-220.00 ug/dL) is too low for an adult male and appears to be a generic/miscalibrated range. Age-banded adult-male 40-49y reference is 45-345 ug/dL (= ~1.2-9.4 umol/L). Values fall progressively in later decades.

references.organization: UCSF Health (Medical Tests Encyclopedia; A.D.A.M./Fischbach-based lab reference)
references.quote: Male (age 40 to 49): 45 to 345 mcg/dL (1.2 to 9.4 umol/L).
Male (age 40 to 49): 45 to 345 mcg/dL. Normal ranges are age- and sex-specific; DHEA-S declines with age.

labPrintedRef: 25.00-220.00 ug/dL (flagged: too low for an adult male; use age-banded 45-345 ug/dL for 40-49y)
why: Adrenal androgen precursor and the most abundant circulating steroid; marker of adrenal androgen production. Screens for adrenal sources of androgen (markedly high in adrenal tumors/CAH) and gives context for overall androgen status. Strongly age-dependent, so the 40-49y band must be used for this ~43y patient.
